verses.1: On that day, Abia son of Yaravam fell ill.
verses.2: And Joram said to his wife, “Come here, and change your clothes. They won’t know that you are Joram’s wife. Go there now; my brother the prophet is speaking to the king about this people.”
verses.3: And you shall take twelve loaves of bread, and they will be cut into pieces. Then you shall put them in a container made of clay. When he comes to you, he will tell you what will happen to the boy.
verses.4: And so, Rebekah did as she was told. She got up and went into her brother’s house. But her brother couldn’t see her, because his eyes were still closed from sleep.
verses.5: And Jehovah said to Ahijah, “Look! Rehoboam’s wife has come to ask you for advice regarding her son. She is very sick. So, speak to her in this manner. Then she will be healed.”
verses.6: And when Ahia heard the sound of her footsteps approaching the door, he said, “Come in! Why are you being honored here? I am the one who has been sent to you.”
verses.7: I have said to Jeremiah, “Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: ‘Because you were raised from among the people, I will declare this against the people of Israel.’”
verses.8: And I will tear the queen from the house of David, and give her to you. Then you shall not be like David’s servants, who obeyed my commands and followed me wholeheartedly in doing only what was right in my eyes.
verses.9: And you refused to do all that was before you. You went and did things that were contrary to God’s will. You created idols to provoke me. You abandoned me after your own way.
verses.10: Therefore, I will bring calamity upon the house of Jeroboam. I will make Jeroboam known as a man who is hidden in a sealed place. He will be left behind in Israel and in my city, after the house of Jeroboam has been destroyed.
verses.11: The dead in Yeravam will be eaten by dogs. The dead in the field will be eaten by birds of the sky. For Jehovah has spoken.
verses.12: And you shall go back to your house, as soon as your feet set foot in the city. And the child will die.
verses.13: And all of Israel reported to him, and they buried him. For it was only then that he could be brought before Yeravam for burial. After all, there were good things found in his body, which were dedicated to the LORD, the God of Israel, in the house of Yeravam.
verses.14: And Jehovah appointed a king over Israel. This king will destroy the house of Jeroboam today, and also in the future.
verses.15: And Jehovah struck Israel when they swore an oath in the waters. He uprooted Israel from this good land that He had given to their ancestors. And he made a river flow across the land, because they did what was pleasing to Jehovah.
verses.16: And he will give Israel because of the sins of Jeroboam, who sinned and led Israel astray.
verses.17: And the wife of Jerubbaal got up and went in. She entered through the door of the house. The boy died.
verses.18: And they buried him, and all of Israel mourned for him, according to what the LORD had commanded through His servant, the prophet Ahijah.
verses.19: And all the words of Jeroboam, who fought and ruled over Israel, are recorded in the book of the days of Israel’s kings.
verses.20: And in the days when Jeroboam ruled for forty-two years, he died and was buried with his ancestors. Then Nadab son of Amasai became king in his place.
verses.21: Rehoboam, son of Solomon, ruled over Judah for forty-one years. During his reign, he ruled in Jerusalem, the city that Jehovah had chosen to place His name upon it, from among all the tribes of Israel. His mother’s name was Naama, the Ammonite woman.
verses.22: And Judah did evil in the eyes of Jehovah. He was angered by all that his ancestors had done in their sins.
verses.23: And they also built shelters for themselves in the mountains and on hills. They settled on every high ground and under every tree.
verses.24: And also, the land was sanctified. All the violations of those nations were punished by Jehovah, as He had decreed before the children of Israel.
verses.25: In the fifth year of King Rehoboam’s reign, Shishak, king of Egypt, attacked Jerusalem.
verses.26: And he took away all the treasures of the House of God, as well as all the treasures of the king’s palace. He took away all the gold objects that Solomon had made.
verses.27: King Rehoboam ordered that metal bars be placed around the door of the king’s palace. He also assigned guards to watch over the entrance to the king’s palace.
verses.28: And when the king entered the Temple of God, the cherubim took him up and brought him back to their place.
verses.29: And all the words of Rehobam, and everything he did, are written in the book of the days of the kings of Judah.
verses.30: And there was war between Rehobam and Yaravham all those days.
verses.31: And Rehuel was buried with his ancestors in the city of David. His mother’s name was Naama the Ammonite. Abiyam, his son, ruled over them.
